the experience of fragility raises the question of whether we are able to remain close to one another when life no longer corresponds to what had been hoped for, and whether we can recognise the work of grace even in situations marked by limits, wounds and apparent failure. in this respect too, the experience of families has something to teach everyone , since fragility belongs to our common human condition and therefore also to the life of the church. we all know the gap between the good we desire and what we are able to live. we need grace, forgiveness and new beginnings to accomplish god’s will, and learn that fidelity is itself a grace to be received and a path to be gradually renewed, often through trial. recognizing this shared challenge should shape the way we accompany one another in the church. what kind of church, then, do people encounter precisely when they are most fragile? do our communities help them discover that they still have a place, a responsibility and gifts to offer? can the truth we proclaim be encountered through the patience, closeness and mercy of our pastoral presence?
